hp_walker.text: Hadrian's Wall, ninety-odd miles from sea to sea, and not one of them flat. I'm having a lovely time. It says so on my blister plaster.
People have been walking this line for two thousand years. Some were in sandals. They had a point.

hp_volunteer.text: Dig down under the granary and you find the timber halls that came after the Romans. Wood over stone. It's the wrong way round, but it's what happened.
After they left, a family built a timber hall inside the old fort. People never really leave a good place. They just change the furniture.

hp_monk.text: Edward I wintered here. He had the whole court in. Imagine the bills. Imagine the bacon.
Lanercost has been repaired and added to many times. Half of it is used as a parish church today. The other half is roofless, which suits some of us.

hp_farmer.text: Bastles are fortified farmhouses: thick walls, a ground floor for the cattle, the family up a ladder. All because the Border Reivers came by night.
Cattle on the ground floor was good for heating and bad for visitors.
